message_1_body:
Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary:
- You are evaluating migration from a hyperscaler-managed inference endpoint to a mix of Dedicated and Private deployments for cost predictability and data isolation.
- Key asks: OpenAI-compatible API surface, parity on prompts, latency and cost comparison vs hyperscaler options, and procurement/security checklist for enterprise review.

Immediate next steps: 
1) We'll run an initial compatibility test (OpenAI-compatible API smoke run) using a small prompt set you provide.
2) We'll run a performance comparison against representative hyperscaler configs (p50/p95 latency for 256/512 token responses, and a cost-per-token estimate).
3) We'll deliver a short comparison PDF + an OpenAI-compat checklist.

Proposed timeline: initial smoke tests by end of day Fri 2026-06-19, perf + cost estimates by Thu 2026-06-25.

Can you confirm a point of contact for procurement and the test prompt set (or a subset) you want us to run? If easiest, drop a 5-10 prompt sample in reply and we'll get started.

Best,
Marissa

message_3_subject: Re: Redwood migration compatibility & hyperscaler comparison - follow-up
message_3_body:
Hey Alex - great questions. Short answers and a concrete proposal below.

OpenAI compatibility and SDK swap:
- We provide an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and an SDK shim that allows the standard OpenAI python/js SDKs to point at our API with minimal changes (base_url + api_key). For the majority of customers it's a config change; a few customers need minor request/streaming tweaks for streaming client behavior.
- To validate this quickly, we can run a drop-in test: you provide a small repo or we use our test harness to replay ~50 representative requests. We'll return a parity report (token-level diffs, any prompt-response mismatches) and a short remediation plan if we see differences.

Performance & hyperscaler comparison (high level):
- Latency: Our Dedicated pools target low p50 latency comparable to hyperscalers on the same GPU class; p95 can vary with batching but we can tune.
- Cost: We typically show 20-45% lower unit cost on equivalent workloads when using reserved/dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler managed endpoints; exact depends on sequence-length distribution and batching.
- Differentiators: smarter KV caching for repeated prompts, transparent cost breakdown in the Console, and migration tooling (OpenAI-compatible endpoints + eval harness).

Proposed tests we'll run: 
1) SDK compatibility smoke run (parity check on ~50 prompts) - deliverable: parity report and small compatibility patch if needed.
2) Latency perf run (p50/p95 for 256/512 tokens) - deliverable: perf metrics and recommended config.
3) Cost estimate for both hosted vs dedicated (1M tokens/month baseline) - deliverable: cost model and suggested reserved capacity commit.

Attachments: I've attached a short comparison PDF and our OpenAI-compat checklist for your procurement team.

Can you confirm: 1) test prompt set (or a pointer to a sample repo), 2) whether we should include procurement on the SDK smoke run, and 3) preferred timeline (we can start the smoke run as soon as tomorrow if you grant sandbox access)?

Best,
Marissa

Attachments:
- redwood-vs-hyperscaler-comparison.pdf
- openai-compat-checklist.xlsx
